stem: A 3-week-old infant has umbilical redness with discharge and the cord has still not separated; which feature is the strongest reason to consider an underlying immunodeficiency or immune dysregulation?

options.text: Delayed umbilical cord separation with omphalitis
A single episode of uncomplicated bronchiolitis

explanation: Delayed umbilical cord separation with omphalitis is the strongest red flag here because it should prompt consideration of an underlying immunodeficiency or immune dysregulation.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because delayed separation of the umbilical cord with omphalitis is a recognised warning sign for possible immunodeficiency or immune dysregulation.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a single uncomplicated episode of bronchiolitis is common and is not, by itself, a strong red flag for immunodeficiency.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because mild evening colic is a common infant behaviour and does not suggest immune dysfunction.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because transient neonatal jaundice that has resolved is not a warning sign for immunodeficiency.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because occasional posseting after feeds is common in young infants and is not suggestive of immune dysregulation.
